12.text: He slept in the house of his master, having neither wife nor home of his own.

16.text: A family of women having no man may live in a camp, depending for

17.text: their subsistence on the herd of the master. Some old women even live singly

18.text: in the camp, having a little house and a few pack-sledges of their own; but

19.text: such existence is hard to bear, and is avoided by younger women, who, if

20.text: left alone in the world, leave their own house, and seek that of another.

30.text: Thus marriage is the normal state of Reindeer Chukchee life, and is even

31.text: the basis of all economical conditions. In this respect the Reindeer Chukchee

32.text: differ from all their neighbors. Among the Maritime portion of the tribe

33.text: marriage is not so indispensable to life, and the unmarried state is somewhat

34.text: more common. Among the Tungus, unmarried men are also more frequently

35.text: met, because marriages there are strictly exogamic, and a bride may be taken

36.text: only from another clan than that of the bridegroom. Moreover, a considerable

37.text: price has to be paid for her.

38.text: In most striking contrast to the Reindeer Chukchee in this respect are

39.text: all the clans of the Russianized Yukaghir living on the Lower Kolyma River.

40.text: These clans are more or less rapidly dying out, some being nearly extinct.
